description: The Energy Follow Up Survey 2011 gives detailed information on how English households use energy at home: the type and use of main and secondary heating, water heating, insulation, lighting, indoor temperatures and appliance use. It was commissioned by the Department of Energy and Climate Change with the Building Research Establishment as a follow-up interview survey of a subset of households from the English Housing Survey 2010-2011, the continuous national survey of housing circumstances, condition and energy efficiency in England; the UK Data Service released version 3 in 2016. A further sub-sample had temperature loggers and electricity monitors installed, and gas and electricity meter readings were collected; raw readings were added in November 2014 as 823 Excel files. Coverage: a subset of English Housing Survey households in England. Access: download from the UK Data Service; linking to the housing survey requires a Secure Access lookup file. Licence: safeguarded data under the End User Licence Agreement; free to registered users. Caveats: a 2011 snapshot; the previous comparable survey was in 1998. Simulation uses are heating patterns, indoor temperatures and appliance use for housing stock energy models. Related records: the EDRP smart meter trials and the England and Wales EPC data.
